scope: The one code commit since round 3 (4e0e3379) answers review round 2's three minor findings. It types the answer's reason as sendOutcome, logs a route line's delivery_status as the role lane's label with the outcome under reason, counts publish_failed and a refused topic publish once per recipient, and moves resolveCoreRoleHolder to an order-free switch. The fingerprint changed, so this is a full round: I ran the soak again and drove every wire answer, the metric and the role lane on real binaries.

notes: A publish_failed send with no registered recipient still adds nothing to envoy_messages_delivered_total; with two recipients it adds 2 failed. The new comment in sendToTopic says this is intended ('a send with no recipient counts nothing'), and the answer itself (504 publish_failed) reaches the sender in both cases.

proof.criterion: A role message through the sending listener is received by the holder or its sender's call errs, with unchanged answers after the outcome retyping
proof.surface: two real envoy-listener binaries built at 4e0e3379, host-a with ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS=1 and host-b without, on one nats-server 2.10.29. Session stand-ins register self_subscribed with no port and receipt forwards the way envoy-client's expectsLaneReceipt does (or never). Driven with curl
proof.command: POST http://127.0.0.1:18381/v1/messages/publish {topic: notifications.role.t4-live|t4-silent|t4-none}, then a btw payload and an unreadable delivery mode ({delivery:{mode:""}})
proof.observed: holder confirms -> 200 with holder ses_holder4 in 57 ms, and a repeat -> 200 with no second forward. Silent holder -> 504 {reason receipt_timeout, holder ses_silent4, attempts 2} in 4.046 s. Each route log line now carries delivery_status as the lane's label and reason as the outcome (delivered/delivered, dedupe/dedupe, receipt_timeout/receipt_timeout, skipped/unclaimed, failed/capability)
proof.negativeControl: unclaimed -> 404 {reason unclaimed}; btw to a holder without it -> 403 {reason capability, holder ses_silent4}; unreadable mode -> 403 {reason capability} 'sent a delivery mode that cannot be read unambiguously'

proof.criterion: The same holds for an ad-hoc topic, with the live topics lane on and off, and inside the window while the hub is down
proof.command: POST /v1/messages/publish {topic: notifications.team.t4} through host-a (lane on) and host-b (lane off), and {topic: notifications.team.nobody}; then the same with the nats-server stopped, reading GET /metrics before and after
proof.observed: lane on and lane off -> 504 {reason not_confirmed, delivered [ses_holder4], undelivered [{ses_silent4, receipt_timeout}]} in 4.03 s; no recipient -> 200 in 33 ms. Hub stopped: 504 {reason publish_failed, 'notifications.team.t4 was not published within 4s: …; no session was sent it'} in 4.036 s, and envoy_messages_delivered_total{delivery_status="failed"} went 2 -> 4 (one per registered recipient). With no recipient, the same 504 publish_failed and the counter stayed at 4. The counter before the outage matched every send: delivered 2, dedupe 1, receipt_timeout 2, failed 2, skipped 5 (one unclaimed plus four live-lane skips)
proof.negativeControl: role send with the hub stopped -> 500 'nats: outbound buffer limit exceeded' in 35 ms (the documented first-read 500); round 1's ad-hoc hub-down answer was 500 after 5.0 s

proof.criterion: The role lane is unchanged by the order-free resolveCoreRoleHolder switch
proof.surface: same rig, a raw core-NATS publish on notifications.role.<role>
proof.command: raw publish of an envelope on notifications.role.t4-silent and notifications.role.t4-none
proof.observed: t4-silent: both listeners forwarded it to ses_silent4, logged 'listener role receipt timed out', and published notifications.envoy.exceptions.notifications.role.t4-silent with delivery exception: receipt_timeout. t4-none: 'listener role has no holder' (skipped), and exceptions with no_holder were published
proof.negativeControl: the raw publish to t4-none, a role nobody holds, was forwarded to nobody and drew the no_holder exception rather than a forward
